senses.title: Before now, by a stated length of time
senses.definition: before the present, used with a stated length of time
senses.definitionCN: 从现在往回数，前面带一个明确的时间长度
senses.example: She left the town two years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她两年前离开了这座城。
senses.why: Ago comes from Old English āgān, 'gone by', so 'two years ago' means two years have gone past since then.
senses.whyCN: ago 来自古英语 āgān「已经过去」，所以 two years ago 就是从那以后两年已经过去了。

senses.title: A long time before now, without exact measure
senses.definition: in the distant past, used without an exact measure of time
senses.definitionCN: 指遥远的过去，不给确切的时间长度
senses.example: Long ago, this street had no tall buildings.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这条街上还没有高楼。
senses.why: The same 'gone by' word is used without a figure in long ago, where the distance back is left vague.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「已经过去」的词，在 long ago 里不跟数字，往回的间隔就留得含糊。

sceneCN: 这里 anything 是「任何事物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是你包里有什么东西吗？

senses.title: Any thing, in questions and negatives
senses.definition: any thing at all, used in questions and negative statements
senses.definitionCN: 用在疑问句和否定句里，指任何一个东西
senses.example: Do you have anything in your bag?
senses.why: Anything is any plus thing, and in a question the speaker does not know whether even one thing is there.
senses.whyCN: anything 是 any 加 thing，在疑问句里说话人连有没有一样东西都不确定。

senses.title: Whatever one chooses
senses.definition: whatever thing is chosen, with no limit
senses.definitionCN: 随便哪一样都可以，不加限制
senses.example: You can choose anything you like.
senses.why: Push 'any one thing' to its limit and every choice is open, so anything means 'whatever you like'.
senses.whyCN: 把「任何一个东西」推到极限，所有选择都打开，anything 就表示「随你选什么」。

senses.title: Definitely not, in anything but
senses.definition: not at all, in the phrase anything but
senses.definitionCN: 在 anything but 中表示完全不是
senses.example: The trip was anything but relaxing.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行一点也不轻松。
senses.why: Anything but literally allows everything except the word that follows, so the phrase ends up meaning 'not that at all'.
senses.whyCN: anything but 字面是「除了后面那个，什么都行」，于是整个短语表示「绝不是那样」。

senses.title: The tall hollow grass with jointed stems

senses.why: Bamboo came into English through Portuguese and Dutch from a Malay word, and it names the tall jointed grass itself.

senses.title: The stems used as a material

senses.definitionCN: 把这种植物的茎当材料使用
senses.example: The fence is made of bamboo.
senses.why: Once the cut stems are used to build or make things, the plant's name also means the material taken from it.
senses.whyCN: 砍下来的竹竿一旦用来搭盖、制作，植物的名字也就指取自它的材料。

senses.title: A container made of woven material
senses.definition: a container made of woven cane, wire or plastic, usually with an open top
senses.definitionCN: 用藤条、铁丝或塑料编成、通常敞口的容器
senses.example: She carried a basket of apples.
senses.why: Basket has long named a container woven from stems, and that open woven shape is the word's centre.
senses.whyCN: basket 一直指用枝条编成的容器，这种敞口编织的形状是它的核心。

senses.title: The amount a basket holds
senses.definition: the amount that a basket contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只篮子所装的分量
senses.example: He picked a whole basket of pears.
senses.why: As with other containers, the basket can stand for one basketful, so a basket of pears means the amount inside.
senses.whyCN: 和别的容器一样，篮子也能代指一篮的量，所以 a basket of pears 说的是里面的分量。

senses.title: The hoop through which a ball is thrown
senses.definition: the ring through which players throw the ball in basketball
senses.definitionCN: 篮球运动中投球要穿过的圆环
senses.example: He threw the ball through the basket.
senses.why: Basketball's first hoops were actual baskets with the bottom removed, so the scoring ring is still called a basket.
senses.whyCN: 篮球最早用的就是去掉底的桃子篮，所以得分的圆环至今仍叫 basket。

definition_en: to begin to be something, or to suit someone
core_image: 一颗种子在土里发芽，慢慢长成一棵小树
scene: 一颗种子在土里发芽，慢慢长成一棵小树。The sky became grey before the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 become 是「变成」（第 01 个义项）；句意是下雨前天色变灰了。

derivatives.zh: 由 become 加 -ing 构成，义为「合适的、好看的」
由 becoming 加 -ly 构成，义为「得体地」

senses.title: To begin to be something
senses.definition: to grow or change into a stated state or role
senses.definitionCN: 转变为某种状态或身份
senses.example: The sky became grey before the rain.
senses.why: Become is be plus come, from Old English becuman, 'to come about, arrive'; a thing that 'comes' into a state has become it.
senses.whyCN: become 由 be 加 come 构成，古英语 becuman 意为「来到、发生」；事物「来到」某种状态，就是变成了它。

senses.title: To suit or look right on someone
senses.definition: to be suitable for someone, or to look right on them
senses.definitionCN: 对某人合适，或穿在身上好看
senses.example: That colour becomes you.
senses.why: What suits a person 'becomes' them in the old sense of fitting well, which is why the word also means 'to look right on'.
senses.whyCN: 合适的东西在旧义里就是与人「相称」，所以这个词也表示穿在身上好看。

senses.title: To happen to, in become of
senses.definition: to happen to someone or something, in the phrase become of
senses.definitionCN: 在 become of 中表示某人某物后来的遭遇
senses.example: What became of the old house?
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子后来怎么样了？
senses.why: Become of asks where something 'came to' in the end, keeping the old 'arrive' picture inside the phrase.
senses.whyCN: become of 问的是某物最后「到了」哪里，短语里仍保留着古老的「到达」画面。

definition_en: earlier than something, or in front of something
core_image: 一列人站在门口排队，最前面的人已经把手放在门上
scene: 门口排着一列人，最前面的人已经把手放在门上。Wash your hands before dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 before 是「在……之前」（第 01 个义项）；句意是晚饭前洗手。

derivatives.zh: 由 before 与 hand 复合，义为「事先」
由 before 与 time 复合，义为「从前」

senses.title: Earlier than a time or event
senses.definition: earlier than a stated time or event
senses.definitionCN: 早于某个时间或事件
senses.example: Wash your hands before dinner.
senses.why: Before is Old English beforan, 'in front of' in place; when two events are lined up, the one in front is the earlier one.
senses.whyCN: before 是古英语 beforan「在前面」；两件事排在一起时，前面的那件就是更早发生的。

senses.title: In front of something in space
senses.definition: in front of someone or something in place
senses.definitionCN: 在某人某物的前方
senses.example: She stood before the door.
senses.why: This is the oldest spatial sense: standing at the front side of a thing, facing it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的空间义：站在某物的正面、面对着它。

senses.title: In the presence of someone in authority
senses.definition: in the presence of a person or body with authority
senses.definitionCN: 出现在有权者或有权威的机构面前
senses.example: He appeared before the judge.
senses.why: To stand before a judge is to stand in his front view, so the space word came to mean appearing in someone's presence.
senses.whyCN: 站到法官前面，就是进入他的视线，于是这个空间词表示在某人面前露面。

senses.title: The two together, before a noun
senses.definition: the two of them together, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 两个一起，放在名词前限定
senses.example: Both children like the story.
senses.exampleCN: 两个孩子都喜欢这个故事。
senses.why: Both goes back to Old English bā þā, 'both those', literally the two taken together, so it includes one and the other.
senses.whyCN: both 来自古英语 bā þā「那两个都」，字面就是把这两个一起拿来，所以它同时包括这一个和那一个。

senses.title: The two, used as a pronoun
senses.definition: the two of them, standing alone as a pronoun
senses.definitionCN: 两个都，单独作代词用
senses.example: Both of them were late.
senses.why: Drop the noun and both stands alone, so the pronoun names the pair without repeating what they are.
senses.whyCN: 把名词省掉，both 就单独站着，代词因此能指那一对，不必再说它们是什么。

senses.title: One and also the other, in both ... and
senses.definition: used in both ... and to join two things that are each true
senses.definitionCN: 在 both ... and 中把两样都成立的事物并列起来
senses.example: She both sings and dances.
senses.why: The 'two together' meaning becomes a joining pattern, so both ... and says that each of the two claims holds.
senses.whyCN: 「两个一起」的意思变成一种并列格式，both ... and 就表示两项陈述都成立。

definition_en: to make something separate, to fail a rule, or to stop for a rest
core_image: 一只掉落的杯子在地上裂开，碎片散在光里
scene: 一只杯子掉在地上裂开，碎片散在光里。Be careful not to break the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 break 是「打破」（第 01 个义项）；句意是小心别打碎玻璃杯。

derivatives.zh: 由 break 加 -able 构成，义为「易碎的」
由 break 加 -er 构成，义为「破坏者、浪花」
由 break 加 -age 构成，义为「破损」
由 break 与 fast 复合，义为「早餐」

senses.title: To separate something into pieces
senses.definition: to make something come apart into pieces
senses.definitionCN: 使完整的东西裂开、碎掉
senses.example: Be careful not to break the glass.
senses.why: Break goes back to Old English brecan and shares its root with Latin frangere, and splitting what was whole is its base.
senses.whyCN: break 来自古英语 brecan，与拉丁语 frangere 同源，把完整的东西弄裂是它的本义。

senses.title: To fail to obey a rule or promise
senses.definition: to fail to keep a rule, law or promise
senses.definitionCN: 不遵守规则、法律或诺言
senses.example: He broke the rule and lost the game.
senses.exampleCN: 他违反了规则，输掉了比赛。
senses.why: A rule is something whole that holds people together; breaking it cracks that hold, so break also means to violate.
senses.whyCN: 规则是维系众人的完整之物，破坏它就是把它弄裂，所以 break 也表示违反。

senses.title: To surpass a record
senses.definition: to go beyond a previous record or limit
senses.definitionCN: 超过原来的纪录或界限
senses.example: She broke the school record in the long jump.
senses.exampleCN: 她打破了学校的跳远纪录。
senses.why: A record is a boundary that has held until now, and passing it breaks that boundary, hence break a record.
senses.whyCN: 纪录是一道守到现在的界限，越过它就是把这界限打破，于是有 break a record。

senses.title: A short pause from work
senses.definition: a short rest from work or activity
senses.definitionCN: 工作或活动中短暂的停顿
senses.example: Let's take a short break.
senses.why: A pause cuts the working time into two, as if breaking it, so the noun break names that gap.
senses.whyCN: 停顿把工作时间切成两段，好像把它弄断，名词 break 就指这段空档。

senses.title: To stop working, of a machine
senses.definition: to stop working properly, said of a machine
senses.definitionCN: 机器不能正常运转
senses.example: The old radio finally broke.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧收音机终于坏了。
senses.why: A machine that stops is like a thing snapped apart inside, so break also describes something no longer working.
senses.whyCN: 机器停转就像内部被折断，所以 break 也描述不能再运转的东西。
